steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Butter a 8 cup souffle dish.
Toast coconut in a non-stick skillet over low heat.

In a medium skillet, melt butter over low heat and add the celery, garlic, curry powder, thyme, red pepper flakes, salt and pepper - cook for 3 minutes. Stir in flour until smooth for about 1 minute. Pour in milk and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil and thickens. Set aside and cool slightly. Whisk the egg yolks one at a time into the sauce. Stir in coconut and crab meat.

In medium bowl, beat egg whites and lemon juice with a mixer until stiff, but not dry. Stir 1/4 of the whites into crab mixture. Quickly and gently fold in the remaining whites. Do not deflate the volume. Transfer mixture to the souffle dish and place it on a rack at the bottom of the oven.
Bake for 30 minutes or until golden, puffed and still moist inside.

review.reviewBody: I made this recipe with fresh crab and it was absolutely phenomenal! Don't be intimidated by the word 'souffle' in the title -- this is the first souffle I have ever made and it turned out beautifully.

Loved it! I cut the recipe in half & I wasn't sure I had enough crab so I added a can of medium shrimp (rinsed). I also used lime juice instead of lemon. With the exception of the salt, I doubled the spices & increased the coconut a bit. Put it all in a 4 cup souffle & baked for 24 minutes. Hubby suggested that, next time, I bake it in individual dishes for a prettier presentation. I served it w/ baked pineapple slices w/ a brown sugar/butter glaze & a romaine salad w/ walnuts & raspberry vinaigrette. I had a bottle of sauvignon blanc open so that's what we had but because of the spiciness of the dish, I think a gewurztraminer would make a better pairing. Thansk Claire...this was very good!

This is a fantastic concept! I made some alterations to adhere to my special diet. I used 1/3 cup of rice milk (I made the recipe for 2), and I used Red Mill Gluten Free All Purpose Baking Flour, a dash of Xanthan Gum (Gluten substitute). I used fresh thyme instead of dried, and used much more curry and garlic. I also added white pepper and garlic pepper. I didn't have red pepper flakes, so I used chili powder. I used extra virgin olive oil instead of butter, and unsweetened coconut flakes instead of sweetened. I topped the dish off with some fresh grated pecorino cheese (an Italian cheese made from ewe's milk). It was fantastic! Because I used a smaller dish, it only took about 10 minutes in the oven. I will definitely try this dish again! Thanks!

This was wonderful. I used a little chive and scallion instead of celery. I added 1/2 tsp. Of old bay. Used ( I pre-cooked it) shrimp and surimi instead of $$crab. Wound up with savory meets a lil sweet. Oh, and I used 1 tsp. Of cream of tartar with the lemon and the egg whites. 
If you never made a souffle... Must have an immersion blender. If you think you're done, give them a bit more.
very good. this was so easy to make!! i used prepackaged, ready to eat lump crab meat (and added a little extra) it was even just as good leftover!

This turned out better than I expected. For my first round I followed the recipe to the letter. I would be curious to hear from other folks that added cheese. Did that improve your experience? Everyone really enjoyed this recipe, and it was easy to make. Next time I might vary the ingredients a little bit to make it slightly spicier.
I omitted coconut flakes, celery tops, red pepper flakes, garlic and substituted dry basil for the oregano. I also sauteed chives with the butter...it turned out delicious!
This was more of a crab quiche. I did not care for it.

The recipe was easy to follow and this turned out good. My family still didn't like it however. I thought that the curry would be subtle since there is only a little bit, but it was all I could taste.
I am a caterer and I planned a function with a Caribbean theme. I served this with a spicy peanut sauce. Outstanding - the line never stopped for this item.
I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out great! Coconut was a very good counterbalance to the savory crab - and enhanced the sweetness of the souffle in a good way.

This was an amazing dish! I was very afraid at first because I was unsure of how it would turn out, but it ended up WAY above expectations! I did change a little bit by adding almost twice the amount of spices, so the flavor was great! My first souffle and I was very pleased with it

Good, but I expected more. With these expensive (crabmeat) and "exotic" (coconut) ingredients, and a fair share of spices, I supposed it would have quite a kick. Nevertheless, it tasted a little too bland for me. Interesting flavour, but seemed to lack something. Also, it was not very "filling". We ended up almost hungry, and a bit disappointed. The souffle part didn't rise very much, but this was because of a rookie mistake of mine - the recipe was not to blame.
Fabulous! What a great combination of flavors. I brought this to a brunch and everyone asked for the recipe. Well written recipe for those scared to attempt a souffle. Do not change a thing !
